'''Carl Hellmuth Hertz''' (also written '''Helmut'''; 15 October 1920 – 29 April 1990) was a German physicist known primarily for being involved in the development of [[inkjet technology]] and [[ultrasound|ultrasound technology]]. He was the son of [[Gustav Ludwig Hertz]] and great nephew of [[Heinrich Hertz]].

== Biography ==
Hellmuth Hertz was born on 15 October 1920 in [[Berlin]], Germany. His father was [[Gustav Ludwig Hertz|Gustav Hertz]] who, along with [[James Franck]], was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel Prize in Physics 1925]] for their experiments on inelastic electron collisions in gases.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/laureates/1925/|title=The Nobel Prize in Physics 1925|date=2014|website=Nobelprize.org|access-date=2017-04-30}}</ref> Gustav Hertz's uncle was in turn [[Heinrich Hertz]], who first conclusively proved the existence of the [[Electromagnetic radiation|electromagnetic waves]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Med fysiken i blodet : en bok om Hellmuth Hertz|last=Westling|first=Håkan|publisher=Bild & Media AB|year=2012|isbn=9789198013603|location=Lund|pages=12–13}}</ref>

Hellmuth graduated from the elite [[Schule Schloss Salem]] boarding school in 1939 at the age of 19 years with the highest grade in mathematics and physics.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Med fysiken i blodet: en bok om Hellmuth Hertz|last1=Westling|last2=Grahm|year=2012|pages=22–23}}</ref> The same year, he was conscripted into the [[German Army (Wehrmacht)]] and served as a soldier for [[Nazi Germany]] in [[World War II]]. In 1943 he was captured in the [[North African theatre (World War II)|North African theatre]] by US troops and brought to America, where he was placed in a [[prisoner-of-war camp]] until 1946. Because his father did some research in the [[Soviet Union]] at that time, he could not get a job in the US. Instead, he got a job at the Department of Physics in [[Lund University]] in Sweden with the assistance of James Franck and the [[Nobel laureate]] [[Niels Bohr]], who were both friends of Gustav Hertz.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Fysik i Lund under 300 år|last=Litzén|first=Ulf|publisher=Lunds universitetshistoriska sällskap|year=2015|isbn=9789175453200|location=Lund|pages=153–155|language=sv}}</ref>

From 1961 he was a teacher at Lund University, and from 1963 he was Professor of Electrical Measurement Technology in Lund. He was involved in the development of both the inkjet and the ultrasound technology.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Fysik i Lund under 300 år|last=Litzén|year=2015|pages=160–163|bibcode=2015filu.book.....L }}</ref> He produced the first [[Echocardiography|echocardiographs]] together with the Swedish physician [[Inge Edler]].<ref>{{cite journal|last2=Goyal|first2=Abha|date=2007|title=The origin of echocardiography: A Tribute to Inge Edler|journal=Tex. Heart Inst. J.|volume=34|pages=431–438|pmc=2170493|pmid=18172524|first1=Siddharth|last1=Singh|number=4}}</ref> He was married to [[Birgit Nordbring-Hertz|Birgit Nordbring]] and was the father of Thomas and [[Hans Hertz (physicist)|Hans Hertz]], and he died on 29 April 1990.
